consolidatedFindings.title: story-024's Flushing freeze is a per-CALL property, not a per-WINDOW one: the shared lastRewardTime is consumed by a window the promo stream did not accrue over, making abort-path promo distribution path-dependent on an unrelated permissionless call

consolidatedFindings.corroborationStrength: HIGHEST OF THE RUN — 5 independent agents, from 5 different starting points (interaction probe, economic schedule analysis, PoC differential, local property derivation, story-criteria check), converged on the same mechanism AND independently agreed on Low. Two of them (code-scanner P4, profiler FixProbeH01::test_probe4_abortFlush_pokeDivergence) reached it with separate, independently-written probes. The convergence is corroboration of the MECHANISM; note it does not by itself argue severity up — all five argue it DOWN to Low, for the same reason (value is conserved).
consolidatedFindings.rootCause: `_updatePool` advances the SHARED clock `lastRewardTime = block.timestamp` unconditionally at L767, OUTSIDE story-024's promo gate at L757. The promo stream has no clock of its own — it shares lastRewardTime with the stable and phUSD streams. The gate therefore suppresses accrual only at the INSTANTS `_updatePool` actually runs, so the freeze is a property of the CALLS made during a flush, not of the flush WINDOW. If nobody pokes `_updatePool` during a flush, lastRewardTime stays pinned at beginFlush and the whole window accrues retroactively at the first post-flush `_updatePool`; if anyone does poke it, that elapsed promo time is discarded for every staker. abortFlush (verified L498-501) neither calls _updatePool nor re-anchors the clock, so the branch is selected by whether an unrelated third party happened to call the permissionless collectReward.
consolidatedFindings.provenance: FIX-INTRODUCED. This defect did not exist before story-024 (d61a7a3): pre-gate, promo accrual across a flush window was continuous and path-INdependent — that was V3-H-01. The gate closed V3-H-01 and introduced this. poc-validator NEW-01 establishes this by differential against pre-fix 69e2a2d; story-faithfulness independently reaches the same conclusion ('a behavioural side effect the gate INTRODUCED and the story did not consider'). This is a fix-introduced Low, not a pre-existing one — material for triage framing, and it is the ONLY residual of an otherwise complete fix.
consolidatedFindings.impactSummary: Distribution-timing non-determinism on the abortFlush path ONLY, decided by an unrelated third party for the cost of gas + 1 wei. NOT a loss and NOT over-emission (refuted twice — see preservedRefutations R3 and REFUT-08-R03): promo is conserved on both branches, the rate is never recomputed in _updatePool, and no capture path exists. Residual harm is (a) distributional — on the no-poke branch the whole window accrues at once over the totalStaked present at unfreeze, so a staker who used pauseWithdraw mid-flush has their share redistributed to survivors; and (b) schedule-integrity — the partner funded Q to incentivise staking across window D and it can be paid instantaneously instead.
quantificationsPreserved: code-scanner P4 (differential, identical timestamps, sole delta = one unrelated collectReward): Branch A (no poke) accPromoPerShare = 0.175e18, promoRewardBalance = 300e18; Branch B (poked) accPromoPerShare = 0.125e18, promoRewardBalance = 500e18. consolidatedFindings.theSingleDisputedQuestion: Is a token-wide freeze/pause of an owner-onboarded partner ERC20 a condition an attacker can EXPLOIT (pattern-matcher: yes — the freeze is the precondition, the permissionless batchClaim is the attacker's action, and burning every staker's promo for gas is the attack), or merely a condition an attacker must WAIT FOR and cannot cause (code-scanner: no unprivileged trigger => Low)? Both are true statements about the same code. The question is whether 'attacker supplies the permissionless call that converts a passive token condition into an irreversible loss' clears the C4 bar for a valid attack path, or whether the external precondition demotes it. econ-scanner sits between: no attacker required at all, the loss happens passively, which is a value leak with stated assumptions (C4 Medium).
whatIsNotDisputed: The mechanism. All three confirm debt-align-before-transfer with no per-user recovery.

That the loss is permanent and on-chain-unrecoverable: `unclaimablePromo` is a WRITE-ONLY aggregate counter — incremented L454, zeroed L487, read NOWHERE in contract logic (code-scanner verified by grep across src/; only other references are the IPhlimboV3.sol:340 getter and NatSpec). PhlimboV3 has no `claimUnclaimable` analogue. Deduplicator re-verified L477-492: finalizePromotion sweeps `retiredToken.balanceOf(address(this))` — the ENTIRE balance including the bank — to leftoverRecipient, then zeroes unclaimablePromo.
That the scalar bank LOSES per-user attribution at bank time, so PromoClaimFailed events are the only record of who is owed.
That abortFlush does not undo it (code-scanner) and does not zero unclaimablePromo (pattern-matcher). Both exits from Flushing destroy the entitlement.

That the project's OWN test asserts this as intended: PhlimboV3Test.t.sol:1676-1686 asserts 'failed amount banked', 'debt still aligned on failure', 'leftover + unclaimable swept', 'unclaimablePromo cleared' — a blocked staker permanently loses her promo to recipient 0x99.

vectorPrecision.CRITICAL: Use code-scanner's CORRECTED precondition. The profiler's LOCAL-101 description is right about the MECHANISM but its implied repro is incomplete, and taking it at face value produces a FALSE NEGATIVE.
vectorPrecision.whyTheNaiveReproFails: A partial pauseWithdraw alone does NOT brick a V2 position: `phUSDDebt` is only written on stake/withdraw/claim, so a user who staked while accPhUSDPerShare == 0 carries debt == 0 and `amount*acc - debt` can never underflow. The first run of probe P9 PASSED (no brick) for exactly this reason — twice.
vectorPrecision.correctPrecondition: Underflow requires a NON-ZERO debt AND a bounded subsequent accumulator move. Debt is frozen at `amount_old * acc_then`; pending is computed as `amount_new * acc_now`. The position is bricked iff `amount_new * acc_now < amount_old * acc_then`, i.e. iff `acc_now / acc_then < amount_old / amount_new`. The user must have interacted at least once at a non-zero accumulator (any user who has ever claimed on a live farm), and the brick persists until the accumulator grows by the inverse of the retained fraction.
vectorPrecision.severityConsequence: This precondition makes the vector MORE dangerous, not less. A user who pauseWithdrew a small slice (retaining ~99%) is bricked only until the accumulator grows ~1.01x — brief. A user who pauseWithdrew MOST of their stake (retaining ~1%) needs a 100x accumulator move and is bricked effectively PERMANENTLY. Severity therefore RISES as the partial exit approaches a full exit — and that same regime is where vector 1a (dust) lives, so the two vectors REINFORCE each other rather than being alternatives. An exact full exit (amount == 0) is safe on both counts: V2._claimRewards returns early and migrate's L173 skip fires.
vectorPrecision.negativeResultValue: The two PASSING revisions of P9 are preserved evidence, not noise: they establish that debt==0 positions and large-accumulator-growth positions are genuinely SAFE. Without them the precondition reads as speculation.

consolidatedFindings.rootCause: The per-user body is unskippable: it skips only on an exactly-zero live V2 position (L173) and has no try/catch, so ANY revert inside the body reverts the whole chunk and pins `migrateIterator` at that index forever. Two independent, confirmed vectors reach that revert, and BOTH are rooted in the same defect — PhlimboV2.pauseWithdraw (PhlimboV2.sol:280-291) reduces `user.amount` while neither enforcing a dust floor nor realigning `phUSDDebt`/`stableDebt`. VECTOR 1a (dust -> V3.stake L188): a V2 position can land in (0, MINIMUM_STAKE=1e15); migrate passes it to `phlimboV3.stake` which reverts 'Below minimum stake' (PhlimboV3.sol:577). V2.withdraw guards this exact case for itself (PhlimboV2.sol:377-379 forces a full exit below MINIMUM_STAKE) — pauseWithdraw does not. VECTOR 1b (stale debt -> V2.withdraw L182): `amount*acc/PRECISION - debt` underflows in V2._claimRewards, which V2.withdraw calls unconditionally; the user's own V2 position is bricked (Panic 0x11) and migrate's unskippable withdraw inherits it.
consolidatedFindings.existenceEvidence: NOT hypothesised — the codebase confirms these positions exist. PhlimboV3's OWN NatSpec (L521-525) names this 'the latent V1/V2 partial-pauseWithdraw brick' and states V3 was written to fix it. Both vectors are pre-existing conditions on the ALREADY-DEPLOYED V2: any partial pauseWithdraw during any V2 pause in V2's history plants them, so such positions may exist on-chain TODAY, before the migration is ever run. Corroborated by ledger V2-L-01 (9ef309e7, open, 'pauseWithdraw stale-debt underflow brick') and V2-L-03 (d6484512, open, 'pauseWithdraw bypasses the MINIMUM_STAKE dust rule') — the two V2-side root defects are ALREADY LEDGERED AS OPEN. This finding is what they cost once the migrator crosses them.
consolidatedFindings.attackVector: Both vectors are self-inflictable and cheap, requiring no owner involvement and no malice — a user emergency-exiting 'most' of their stake during any V2 pause plants either one by accident. As a deliberate grief, vector 1a costs ~1 wei: `pauseWithdraw(position - 1)`. When the owner later runs the migration, the pass advances until index k and reverts forever; every user at index >= k is stranded in V2.
consolidatedFindings.noRecoveryProof: There is NO in-contract recovery, PoC-verified on all three candidate escapes: (1) a larger `maxIterations` does not skip — the loop always restarts at `migrateIterator` (L163) and re-hits index k; (2) `seedUsers` requires `!seeded || migrateIterator == -1` (L126) and the iterator is wedged at k, so the owner cannot reseed a list excluding the bad address — it reverts 'Pass in progress'; (3) `withdrawAll` is a pure balance sweep that deliberately does not reset the pass (L243-265).
consolidatedFindings.ownerWorkaroundPreserved: Undocumented and invasive, which is why this is reported rather than dismissed. Vector 1a: owner can `phlimboV2.setMigrator(<ownerEOA>)`, `phlimboV2.withdraw(dust, dustUser)` as the EOA-migrator to drive the position to 0 so the skip fires, then re-wire — confiscating the user's dust into the owner EOA pending manual return, repeated per user, temporarily un-wiring the live migrator. Vector 1b RESISTS EVEN THAT: V2.withdraw is the very call that underflows, so the owner-as-migrator hits the same revert; the position can only be cleared by pausing V2 and having the USER pauseWithdraw the remainder to exactly zero (pauseWithdraw is strictly msg.sender-only and not delegatable) — i.e. recovery requires that specific user's cooperation. This asymmetry matters for severity: 1b's recoverability is strictly worse than 1a's, and the 'owner can just redeploy' argument that caps this at Medium is the ONLY remaining escape for 1b.

The natural remediation action — rotate out of the broken promo, which is exactly what V3-M-02's own ledger description names as the recovery — is precisely the one that destroys the entitlements irreversibly, silently, and with no revert or warning. impactFaceA_orderingReallocation.claim: withdrawAll sweeps the entire balance while leaving every `unclaimable` entry intact, and — unlike MigratorV1V2 — deliberately does NOT abort the pass, so migration RESUMES and re-funds the contract with LATER users' banked rewards. Because claimUnclaimable pays first-come-first-served out of the common balance, a user whose claim was already de-funded by the sweep can drain a later user's legitimately-backed rewards. The unbacked-ness MIGRATES BY CLAIM ORDERING rather than staying with the users who were banked at sweep time.
impactFaceA_orderingReallocation.pocResult: alice banks 2500e18 (blocklisted) -> owner withdrawAll sweeps to owner, alice's entry STILL READS 2500e18 -> pass resumes, bob banks 2500e18 legitimately (contract balance now 2500e18) -> alice unblocks and claims FIRST, receiving 2500e18 that were BOB's -> bob's claimUnclaimable REVERTS despite his entry still reading 2500e18.
impactFaceA_orderingReallocation.netEffect: Value is conserved overall (the owner holds the swept funds), so this is a REALLOCATION and an operational-record hazard, not net destruction.
impactFaceA_orderingReallocation.theSubtleHarm: PRESERVED VERBATIM FROM ECON-08-003 because it is the part a reader will miss: the earlier user's mapping entry is now ZEROED — so an owner reconciling from the LIVE MAPPING sees them as settled and reimburses only the later user (self-correcting), whereas an owner reconciling from the at-sweep RewardForwardFailed EVENT SNAPSHOT reimburses the earlier user a SECOND time (double-pay). The live mapping and the event history disagree about who is owed, and the NatSpec tells the owner to perform exactly this reconciliation without saying which source to trust.

impactFaceB_invisibility.claim: story-025 introduced a new class of contract-held liability (per-user banked `unclaimable`) with NO aggregate accounting: no `totalUnclaimable[token]`, no aggregate view, no enumeration. The owner therefore CANNOT determine, before or after calling withdrawAll, WHETHER the sweep stranded anything or WHOM to reimburse — the 'out-of-band owner obligation' the NatSpec assigns them is not dischargeable from on-chain state alone (it requires off-chain RewardForwardFailed replay, netted against UnclaimableClaimed).
impactFaceB_invisibility.law3Analysis: PRESERVED — the distinction is load-bearing and the finding is invalid without it. The DESIGN CHOICE (unconditional sweep) is deliberate, documented, and strictly MORE generous than the house baseline; Law 3 trusts it and this finding does NOT contest it. The SURPRISE is the INVISIBILITY. PhlimboV3 exposes its banked liability as the aggregate view `unclaimablePromo()` and SolvencyDetermination.md §5 elevates it to a term any observer can check; the migrator copied the helper but NOT the liability-accounting discipline, and is absent from the solvency doc entirely. An owner sweeping dust after a completed pass — withdrawAll's original innocuous purpose, still asserted verbatim at L239 — has no on-chain signal that anything is owed, and the resulting failed claim surfaces to the user as a generic ERC20 insufficient-balance revert, not as 'swept'. Surprise => footgun => in scope as an operational hazard.

consolidatedFindings.rootCause: `_tryTransfer` does `address(token).call(...)` and returns `callSuccess && (returndata.length == 0 || abi.decode(returndata,(bool)))`. consolidatedFindings.title: seedUsers replaces the user list WHOLESALE in one unchunkable transaction (O(N) delete + O(N) push), so a sufficiently large V2 user base cannot be seeded or re-seeded at all

consolidatedFindings.rootCause: `seedUsers` does `delete users` (an O(N) storage clear of the previous list) followed by an O(N) push loop, all in one unchunkable transaction. The list can only be replaced WHOLESALE — no append mode, no chunked seed. A user base large enough to exceed the block gas limit in either the clear or the push cannot be seeded at all, and cannot be reseeded for the straggler second pass.
consolidatedFindings.quantificationPreserved: Post-London refunds are capped at 20% of gas used, so `delete users` nets ~2.9k gas/slot. ~5,000 users clears in roughly 11-12M gas (fits in a 30M block); the ceiling is on the order of ~12-15k users. Whether this binds depends ENTIRELY on the real V2 user count — likely well under the limit for this protocol, which is why severity is Low. NOTE: this is the THIRD severity determination this run gated on an unstated deployment fact (cf. DEDUP-08-05's token decimals, DEDUP-08-06/DEDUP-04's APY). The V2 user count is knowable on-chain and would settle it.

refutations.claim: A third party can force a staker's promo forward to fail (gas-griefing the permissionless batchClaim via the 63/64 rule), then let the owner's rotation confiscate the banked amount.

refutations.evidence: probe-08-code.t.sol::test_P1_gas_grief_batchClaim (gas 30k-400k, 2k steps) and probe-08-code2.t.sol::test_P1b_gas_grief_fine_sweep (gas 20k-1,000,000, 500-gas steps). Across the WHOLE band there is NO gas value at which the outer batchClaim frame survives while the inner _tryTransfer OOG-fails: 'gas where grief lands = 0'. First gas at which batchClaim succeeds = 80,000, and from there the transfer always succeeds too.

To starve a ~50k-gas ERC20 transfer the attacker must leave ~50k at the call site, reserving only ~780 gas for the outer frame — far below the ~30k of post-call work batchClaim still must do (the unclaimablePromo SSTORE, PromoClaimFailed, the flushCursor SSTORE, FlushProgress). refutations.claim: MigratorV2V3.claimUnclaimable can be griefed, or banked amounts can be double-paid / double-banked on the straggler second pass.
refutations.analysis: (a) Grief: `unclaimable[token][msg.sender]` is keyed per-caller, so no third party can zero another user's entry; nonReentrant. (b) The CEI ordering at L230-231 is not merely correct, it is PROTECTIVE: because the entry is zeroed BEFORE the transfer, a transfer that reverts (e.g. the user is still blocked, or withdrawAll left the claim unbacked) reverts the whole tx and unwinds the zeroing — the claim SURVIVES to be retried. There is no zero-then-fail loss window. (c) Double-bank: `_forward` banks exactly one measured delta per token per user per iteration, and pay/bank are mutually exclusive branches (L287-288). A duplicate address in the seed list is harmless — the second visit live-reads amount == 0 and hits the `continue` at L173. (d) Cross-user contamination: the balance bracket (L175-196) is delta-based, so one user's banked tokens sitting in the migrator appear in BOTH `before` and `after` and cancel exactly; they never leak into another user's computed delta. (e) Permanent stranding: only via withdrawAll, explicitly documented as an accepted trade-off at L63-68 and an obvious owner action (Law 3 — not a footgun).
refutations.corroboration: pattern-matcher independently refuted the same two claims (explicitlyRefuted 'double-bank on retry pass' and 'CEI / reentrancy on the pull leg'), reaching identical conclusions by identical reasoning. Two agents, independent.

R4(e) refutes the BASE stranding case (same boundary as REFUT-08-R02); the ordering/resume aspect is untouched.

refutations.subject: explicitlyNotFindings (4 items) — considered and REJECTED, preserved so a future run does not re-derive them
items: story-024 gate composition with startPromotion — VERIFIED SAFE. startPromotion calls _updatePool() BEFORE assigning promoToken (and finalize zeroes promoToken), so a stale lastRewardTime spanning a flush window cannot retro-accrue against the NEXT promo token. 'This was the most plausible way to reintroduce V3-H-01 and it is closed.'

story-025 trade-off (b) (_forward banking) — VERIFIED SAFE. The debt is NOT signal-only (`unclaimable(address,address)` is a public view, IMigratorV2V3.sol:122); backed 1:1 by construction; balance-diff bracketing not corrupted; banked entries keyed by token ADDRESS so a promo rotation does not orphan a claim; reentrancy-safe; strictly better than the reverting alternative it replaced. CAVEAT PRESERVED: '(b)'s safety is CONDITIONAL on (a) not being exercised — the banked debt's only backing is the contract balance that withdrawAll can zero. That composition is exactly what DEDUP-08-09 tracks.'

withdrawAll's new external call to phlimboV3.promoToken() coupling the escape hatch to V3's liveness — REJECTED. phlimboV3 is immutable and set to a real V3 at construction; promoToken() is a plain public getter that cannot realistically revert.

claimUnclaimable's arbitrary `token` parameter — REJECTED. unclaimable[token][msg.sender] can only be non-zero for phUSD/rewardToken/promoToken, and amount==0 reverts, so an attacker-supplied token address is inert. (Independently reached by story-faithfulness's own acceptance criterion and consistent with R4.)
